doc.title: Pete Jolly interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Playing on Herb Alpert, Sinatra and other pop records
summary: Jolly recalls double-piano with Burt Bacharach on This Guy's in Love with You and other hit dates.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Wait a minute now. Are you the guy that played [scats]. On “This Guy’s In Love with You” on the record?
Well there were two pianos. It was Burt and I playing. It was Burt Bacarach and I, yeah. I don’t remember — I think we were both doing the same thing.
There were two pianos on the date, right.
And “A Taste of Honey,” I was on that one.
Oh, with Herb Alpert? © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-
I was on “New York New York” with Frank.
You’ve played some significant little piano riffs then.
I’m trying to think of the list of — you get my bio out — but there were a lot of different record dates with all kinds of different artists. Dean Martin, Bing Crosby, through the year.
